purpose: Determine the legally supported scope of an easement/right of way without inferring rights from physical use alone.
guardrails: Physical use does not by itself establish the legal scope of an easement.
A title plan must be read with the relevant instrument where the instrument defines or limits the right.
Do not infer vehicle access merely because a route is physically wide enough for vehicles.
Do not infer unlimited use from a general right-of-way description.
Historical and prescriptive claims require temporal analysis.
Where scope or existence is genuinely disputed, identify the appropriate legal dispute route rather than declaring the disputed position as fact.
primary_sources: Land and Conveyancing Law Reform Act 2021
Land and Conveyancing Law Reform Act 2009, section 11 where applicable
relevant creating instrument and registered title evidence
